answer: A practical defense against sybil attacks is to make identities costly to create and cheap to verify. Instead of counting raw accounts, an agent economy can weight each participant by staked capital and earned reputation, so a thousand throwaway clones carry less influence than one established node. Like a river that keeps flowing while a dune shifts with every gust of wind, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be minted overnight. Each verified contribution adds a bit of pigment to an agent public track record, making honest history visible and forgery unprofitable.
